_about: Transition drift T @ E - E (the product divided by the row sums of T first when normalizeRows), for cellucid-python's compute_transition_drift and cellucid-r's cellucid_transition_drift(). Written by cellucid-python's scripts/generate_transition_drift_conformance.py with exact rational arithmetic, independently of both. Matrices are row-major; a sparse transition matrix is 0-based coordinates in row-major order. An exact case is computed without rounding up to the division and the subtraction, so bound is 0 and the drift is matched bit for bit; a general case gives the exact drift rounded to float64 and, per value, a bound twice the forward error of the computation in any summation order: 2 (2n + 3) u (A / s + |E|) with u = 2**-53, n cells, A = |T| @ |E| and s the row sum (1 without normalization). An implementation passes when |drift - expected| <= bound for every value, with the matrix given dense and given sparse.

cases.name: exact, dense, one column, as given
exact, sparse, an empty row, as given
exact, sparse, ten columns, rows normalized
general, sparse, coordinates in the ten thousands
